name: type-lines
summary: Headline or paragraph rises line by line from behind a mask, once, measured from the real layout.

name: type-scrub
summary: Statement whose words go from muted to full colour in reading order as it scrolls through; reversible, no pinning.

name: marquee-type
summary: Oversized looping line of text with scroll-velocity nudge, pause button, and static wrapped fallback.

name: pinned-chapters
summary: Sticky media column cross-fades to the chapter crossing mid-screen, with a linked progress list; stacked on phones.

name: horizontal-rail
summary: Row of cards moves sideways as the page scrolls down a tall section; keyboard reachable; native snap strip on phones.

name: image-sequence
summary: Scroll-scrubbed canvas over numbered frames with progressive loading and HTML captions; poster fallback.

name: photo-reveal
summary: Images open with a clip-path wipe while the picture settles inside a fixed frame; per-item direction, small stagger, optional gentle inner parallax, zero layout shift.

name: cursor-trail
summary: Images or token shapes follow the pointer with spring lag in one area, or a list row's preview follows the pointer and docks beside the focused row; off on touch and reduced motion.

name: page-curtain
summary: Page-to-page transition for multi-page static sites: cross-document View Transitions with a token-coloured curtain fallback, focus and title announcement handled.

name: shader-ground
summary: Animated WebGL ground behind a hero or band: slow noise between background, primary and accent tokens; variants flow, contour, grid, caustic; optional token scrim behind text; CSS gradient fallback.

name: shader-orb
summary: Raymarched signed-distance object (blob, twisted torus, crystal, liquid) in one fragment shader, token-lit, turning with pointer and section scroll; adaptive resolution; CSS sphere fallback.

name: particle-field
summary: Thousands of soft points in a curl-noise flow that dodge the pointer and gather into a word from the page (or an SVG path) as the section crosses mid-screen; word stays as real text.
